sub: Named after the single letter Qāf that opens ayah 1
theme: The Hereafter. Quraysh called rising from dust impossible. The surah answers with creation, history and Allah’s complete knowledge, then shows death, the Judgement, Hell and Paradise as if they were already happening.
story: Revealed in Makkah. No report fixes the date, but the content fits the middle Makkan years, around the fifth year of prophethood, when opposition was fierce but had not yet become open persecution.

What shocked Quraysh most was the idea of rising again after the body turns to dust. They called it impossible. The surah answers: Allah knows every scattered part, records every word, and will bring everyone out at one call, like plants rising after rain.

The Prophet ﷺ gave it special weight. He recited it in the Eid prayer, often in Fajr, and so regularly in the Friday sermon that a neighbour, Umm Hishām, memorised it just from hearing him. It opens the Mufaṣṣal, the Quran’s final section.

sections.title: Deniers call a warner and resurrection strange; Allah knows what earth consumes
sections.meaning: Allah swears by the glorious Quran. The deniers are amazed that a warner came from among them, and call rising again after turning to dust a far-fetched return. Allah knows what the earth eats away of them, and a preserved Book holds it all. They denied the truth, so they are confused.
points: Qāf; an oath by the glorious Quran
Amazed that a warner came from among themselves
Rising after dust? A far-fetched return
Allah knows what the earth takes; a preserved Book
They denied the truth, so they are confused
sections.matters: It states the whole problem the surah answers: denying the Prophet ﷺ and denying resurrection. The reply comes at once: a body that turns to dust is never lost to Allah’s knowledge.
sections.story: No specific incident. The Makkans could not see how bodies turned to dust could live again, and kept changing what they called the Prophet ﷺ: a sorcerer, then a poet, then a soothsayer.
explained: Qāf is one of the single letters that open some surahs. Allah swears by al-Qurʾān al-majīd, the glorious Quran, vast in meaning and blessing. The deniers were amazed that the warner was a man from among them, whose family and honesty they knew, and called it ʿajīb, strange.

Their real objection was rising again: after we die and turn to dust, we come back? Far-fetched. Allah answers that He knows exactly what the earth eats of their flesh and bones, and a kitāb ḥafīẓ, a preserved Book, holds everything. They denied the truth, so they are in amr marīj: muddled, jumping from one claim to another.
teaches: Being amazed at the truth is no excuse for rejecting it.
Even as scattered dust, nothing of you is lost to Allah.
Rejecting the truth leaves a person confused and inconsistent.
Allah swears by the Quran, so honour it.
sections.hook: The surah opens on page 518 with the single letter Qāf. Ayah 2 says ‘amazed’ twice: ʿajibū, then ʿajīb. Ayah 3 ends on ‘baʿīd’ (far); baʿīd returns in 27 and 31.

sections.title: Sky, earth and rain show resurrection; eight nations denied and were punished
sections.meaning: Look at the sky, built without a crack, and the earth, spread out with mountains and beautiful plants. Rain grows gardens, grain and palms, and revives dead land: that is how the dead will come out. Eight nations denied and were punished. The first creation did not tire Allah, so why doubt a second?
points: The sky: built, adorned, with no cracks
The earth: spread, mountains, beautiful plants; insight for whoever turns back
Rain grows gardens, grain and palms; dead land lives: so is the coming out
Eight nations denied their messengers; the threat came true
Did the first creation tire Us? They doubt a new one
sections.matters: This is the surah’s evidence. It answers “a far-fetched return” three ways: the creation all around, dead land coming back to life after rain, and the nations who denied before. If the first creation did not tire Allah, repeating it is easier.
sections.story: No specific incident. Naming the earlier nations warned Quraysh they could meet the same end, and comforted the Prophet ﷺ: every one of those nations had rejected its messenger too.
explained: They only need to look up. The sky is built without pillars, decorated with stars, with no furūj, not a crack or flaw. The earth is spread out, held firm by mountains, and covered with every bahīj, beautiful, kind of plant. All of it is insight and a reminder for the ʿabd munīb, the servant who turns back to Allah.

Blessed rain grows gardens, harvest grain and tall palms heavy with layered fruit. It revives dead land: kadhālika al-khurūj, that is how you will come out of the graves. Nūḥ’s people, ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh, Lūṭ’s people and others denied, and the threat struck them. Did the first creation wear Allah out? No, and repeating it is easier.
teaches: Look at creation with a heart that turns back to Allah.
Dead land turning green after rain is a picture of resurrection.
Denying one messenger is like denying them all.
The One who created the first time can easily create again.
sections.hook: ‘Anbatnā’ (We made grow) comes in ayat 7 and 9. The nations run three, three, then two across ayat 12–14. ‘Al-khurūj’ (the coming out) ends ayah 11 and returns in ayah 42.

sections.title: Allah knows every whisper, angels write every word; then death and resurrection
sections.meaning: Allah created man and knows what his soul whispers to him; He is nearer to him than his jugular vein. Two angels, right and left, record every word. Then the daze of death arrives, the Horn is blown, and each soul comes with a driver and a witness. The cover lifts, and the heedless see.
points: Allah knows the soul’s whispers; nearer than the jugular vein
Two angels, right and left, record every word
Death’s daze comes: what you ran from
The Horn; each soul with a driver and a witness
You were heedless; the cover is lifted, sight is sharp
sections.matters: Section 2 showed Allah can raise the dead. This one makes it personal: He already knows your thoughts, your words are being written now, and death is certain. No one is left unwatched or unaccountable.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the answer to those who thought they could live as they pleased, with no one watching and no account to give.
explained: Allah made man and knows even what his soul whispers to him. He is nearer than ḥabl al-warīd, the jugular vein, either by His knowledge or through His angels. Two angels stay with each person, the one on the right writing good deeds and the one on the left writing bad ones. Not one word escapes them.

Then comes sakrat al-mawt, the overwhelming daze of death: this is what you kept running from. The Horn is blown for the Day of the threat. Every soul arrives with a sāʾiq driving it and a shahīd testifying about it. You were heedless; now the cover is removed and your sight is sharp, but too late to help.
teaches: Allah knows your thoughts before they become words.
A single word can earn Allah’s pleasure or His anger.
Death can’t be escaped, only prepared for.
Heedlessness now becomes painful clarity later.
sections.hook: Two pairs stay with each person: two recorders on the right and left (17), then a driver and a witness (21). ‘Wa jāʾat’ (and there came) opens both ayah 19 and ayah 21.

sections.title: His record presented, the stubborn thrown into Hell; his devil disowns him
sections.meaning: His companion angel brings what he has ready. Allah orders: throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever who blocked good, transgressed, doubted and set up another god. His devil companion protests that he never made him rebel. Allah ends the dispute: the warning came long ago, His word does not change, and He wrongs no one.
points: The companion: here is what I have, ready
Throw in Hell the stubborn, the blocker of good, the doubter, the idolater
The devil: I did not make him rebel
Don’t argue before Me; the warning came; I wrong no one
sections.matters: On that Day every excuse collapses. The record is ready, even the devil blames the man, and Allah’s justice is stated plainly: the warning came in advance, so no one is punished without proof.
sections.story: Reportedly, ayah 26 was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, and ‘blocker of good’ meant he kept his nephews from Islam. Otherwise no specific incident; the Judgement scene simply continues.
explained: The qarīn, the angel assigned to the person, says: here he is, and his record is ready. Allah tells the two angels, alqiyā, throw into Jahannam every kaffār ʿanīd: stubborn in disbelief, blocking good such as zakah, transgressing, doubting, and worshipping another god beside Allah. Throw him into the severe punishment.

Then his other companion, the devil, speaks: “Our Lord, I did not make him rebel; he went far astray himself.” The man blames the devil, and the devil blames the man. Allah ends it: do not argue before Me. I sent the warning ahead through the messengers. My word does not change, and I am never unjust to My servants.
teaches: Your record will be ready; fill it with good now.
Blocking good, transgressing and doubting lead to ruin.
Shayṭān will disown everyone who followed him.
Excuses won’t work on that Day; the warning has already come.
Allah is never unjust to anyone.
sections.hook: ‘Qāla qarīnuhu’ (his companion said) comes twice, in 23 and 27. ‘Alqiyā’ (throw, you two) comes in 24 and 26, around the list of sins. ‘Ladayya’ appears in 23, 28 and 29.

sections.title: Hell asks “Any more?”; Paradise comes near the righteous, with even more
sections.meaning: Hell is asked, “Are you full?” and replies, “Is there any more?” Paradise is brought close to the righteous. It is for everyone who kept returning to Allah and guarded His commands, who feared the Most Merciful unseen and came with a turning heart. Enter in peace, with all you wish and more.
points: Hell: are you full? Is there any more?
Paradise brought near the righteous, not far
For the awwāb and ḥafīẓ who feared the Most Merciful unseen
Enter in peace: the Day of forever
All they wish, and with Us more
sections.matters: The two destinations side by side. Then it lists exactly who Paradise is for: those who keep returning to Allah, guard His commands, fear Him in private and bring a heart turned toward Him.
sections.story: No specific incident. It completes the Judgement scene, turning from those thrown into Hell to those welcomed into Paradise.
explained: Allah asks Hell, “Are you full?” It answers, “Hal min mazīd?” Either it wants more, until Allah places His Foot on it and it says, “Enough, enough!”, or it means it is full, with no room left. Then Paradise is brought close to the muttaqīn, near enough to see before they enter.

It is promised to every awwāb, who keeps turning back to Allah in repentance, and ḥafīẓ, who guards His commands. They feared ar-Raḥmān bil-ghayb, in private where no one saw, and came with a qalb munīb, a heart turned to Him. “Enter in peace”: safe forever. They get whatever they wish, and mazīd, more, reported to include seeing Allah.
teaches: Fear Allah in private, where only He sees you.
Keep returning to Allah after every slip.
Guard what Allah commanded and the limits He set.
Paradise holds more than anyone can think to wish for.
sections.hook: The section opens and closes on ‘mazīd’ (more): Hell’s ‘hal min mazīd’ (30) and ‘wa ladaynā mazīd’ (35). ‘Ḥafīẓ’ (32) echoes ayah 4, and ‘munīb’ (33) echoes ayah 8.

sections.title: Destroyed nations found no escape; be patient, glorify, listen for the Caller
sections.meaning: Stronger nations were destroyed and found no escape: a reminder for any listening heart. Allah made the heavens and earth in six days without tiring. So be patient, glorify Him morning, evening and night, and listen for the Caller. Allah knows what they say; remind with the Quran.
points: Stronger nations found no escape: a reminder for a listening heart
Heavens and earth in six days, with no tiredness
Be patient; glorify before sunrise and sunset, at night, after prayer
Listen: the Caller from near, the Blast, the Day of coming out
We give life and death; the earth splits; gathering is easy
We know what they say; you can’t force them: remind
sections.matters: The conclusion gathers the surah’s proofs, history (36), creation (38) and the rising (41–44), then turns to the Prophet ﷺ: bear their words, keep worshipping, and remind with the Quran. Forcing faith was never his job.
sections.story: Reportedly, ayah 38 answered some Jews who claimed Allah rested on the seventh day. Another report says people asked the Prophet ﷺ to warn them, and ayah 45’s ending came down. The command to be patient came before fighting was ordered.
explained: How many generations, stronger than Quraysh, roamed and built across the land, yet found no maḥīṣ, no escape, when punishment came? That is a lesson for anyone with a living heart, or who listens with full attention. Allah made the heavens, the earth and all between in six days, and no lughūb, no tiredness, touched Him.

So bear what they say, and glorify your Lord before sunrise and sunset, at night and after prayers. Listen for the Caller, calling from near: the Blast, the Day of coming out. The earth splits and they rush out; gathering them is easy for Allah. You can’t force them to believe, so remind with the Quran whoever fears the warning.
teaches: Strength and wealth did not save nations who denied.
Listen to the Quran with a present heart.
Patience grows from glorifying Allah morning and evening.
Guard the prayers before sunrise and before sunset.
Our job is to remind; guidance belongs to Allah.
sections.hook: The surah opens with ‘wal-Qurʾān al-majīd’ (1) and closes with ‘fa-dhakkir bil-Qurʾān’ (45). ‘Wa laqad khalaqnā’ opens 38, as it opened 16. ‘Dhālika yawmu’ comes a third time in 42, after 20 and 34.

groups.text: Qāf. By the glorious Quran, the deniers are amazed a warner came from among them, and call rising from dust far-fetched.
Allah knows what the earth eats of them and keeps a preserved Book. They denied the truth, so they are confused.
The flawless sky, the spread-out earth, its mountains and beautiful plants: insight for every servant who turns back to Allah.
Blessed rain grows gardens, grain and tall palms, and revives dead land. That is how the dead will come out.
Eight nations before Quraysh denied their messengers, so Allah’s threat came true against them.
Was Allah worn out by the first creation? No, yet they doubt a new creation.
Allah knows the soul’s whispers and is nearer than the jugular vein; two angels record every word.
The daze of death comes with the truth, then the Horn is blown: the Day of the threat.
Every soul comes with a driver and a witness. The cover is lifted and sight becomes sharp.
The companion angel presents what he has ready: throw into Hell every stubborn, good-blocking, doubting idolater.
The devil disowns the man. Allah says: don’t argue before Me; the warning came, and I wrong no one.
Hell is asked if it is full and says “Any more?”; Paradise is brought near the righteous.
It is promised to everyone who turns back to Allah, guards His commands, and fears the Most Merciful unseen.
Enter in peace, forever. They get whatever they wish, and Allah has more.
Stronger nations were destroyed and found no escape: a reminder for a heart that listens.
Allah made the heavens and earth in six days without tiring. So be patient and glorify Him, day and night.
Listen for the Caller from a near place, and the Blast: the Day of coming out.
Allah gives life and death. The earth splits and they rush out; gathering them is easy for Him.
Allah knows what they say. You can’t force them, so remind with the Quran whoever fears His warning.

1.explain: Qāf is one of the single letters that open some surahs; Allah knows what He means by it. He swears by al-Qurʾān al-majīd: the glorious Quran, vast in meaning and full of good.

2.explain: Bal ʿajibū: they were amazed that the mundhir, the warner, was one of them, a man whose family and honesty they knew. They called it ʿajīb, strange, when the real wonder is their reaction.

3.explain: Their objection: after dying and turning to dust, we come back? Rajʿun baʿīd: a far-fetched return that will never happen. They measured Allah’s power against their own weakness.

4.explain: Allah knows exactly what the earth eats away of their flesh, bones and hair, and where every part went. A kitāb ḥafīẓ, a preserved Book, holds it all, safe from any change.

5.explain: The real cause: they denied the truth when it came. So they are in amr marīj, a muddled state, calling the Prophet ﷺ a sorcerer, then a poet, then a soothsayer, never settling on anything.

6.explain: Have they not looked at the sky above them? Built without pillars, adorned with stars, with no furūj: no cracks, gaps or flaws. Making that is greater than raising people again.

7.explain: The earth: spread out wide, pinned with rawāsī, firm mountains that stop it shaking, and grown with every bahīj kind of plant, a joy to look at.

8.explain: Tabṣirah, insight, and dhikrā, a reminder, for the ʿabd munīb: the servant who turns back to Allah with love, fear and hope. The one who turns away gains nothing from the signs.

9.explain: Mubārak rain, blessed and full of good, comes down and grows gardens and ḥabb al-ḥaṣīd: grain that is harvested, such as wheat and barley.

10.explain: …and bāsiqāt, tall palm trees, with ṭalʿ naḍīd: fruit clusters packed in layers, one over another.

11.explain: Food for Allah’s servants. The same rain brings dead land back to life. Kadhālika al-khurūj: that is exactly how people will come out of their graves.

12.explain: Before Quraysh, Nūḥ’s people denied and were drowned in the flood; so did aṣḥāb ar-Rass, a people who lived by a well and worshipped idols, and Thamūd, the people of Ṣāliḥ.

13.explain: …and ʿĀd, the people of Hūd, and Pharaoh, the tyrant king of Egypt, and ikhwān Lūṭ, the people Lūṭ was sent to.

14.explain: …and aṣḥāb al-Aykah, the people of the thicket, sent Shuʿayb, and the people of Tubbaʿ, a king of Yemen. All denied their messengers, so the threat came true. Denying one messenger is denying them all.

15.explain: A-fa-ʿayīnā: were We worn out by the first creation? No. They are in labs, confused doubt, about a new creation, though making something again is easier than making it first.

16.explain: Allah made man and knows what his soul whispers to him, though passing thoughts are forgiven until spoken or acted on. He is nearer than ḥabl al-warīd, the jugular vein: by His knowledge, or through His angels.

17.explain: Al-mutalaqqiyān: the two angels who take in every deed, one sitting on the right writing good deeds, one on the left writing bad ones. They stay with a person constantly.

18.explain: Not one word leaves his mouth without a raqīb ʿatīd, a watcher ready to record it. A single word can win Allah’s pleasure, or His anger, until the Day a person meets Him.

19.explain: Sakrat al-mawt, the overwhelming daze of death, comes with the truth no one can deny: “This is what you kept running from.” Even the Prophet ﷺ, as he died, said death has its agonies.

20.explain: The Horn is blown for the resurrection. Dhālika yawmu al-waʿīd: that is the Day the threat is carried out on the wrongdoers, and the promise kept for the believers.

21.explain: Every soul arrives with a sāʾiq, an angel driving it to the gathering, and a shahīd, a witness to its deeds: another angel, or in another view the person’s own hands and feet.

22.explain: You were heedless of this. Now the ghiṭāʾ, the cover over your heart and eyes, is removed, and your sight is sharp. You clearly see what you denied, but it no longer helps.

23.explain: His qarīn, the angel assigned to him, says: here is what I have, ready. He brings the person and his record, nothing added and nothing left out.

24.explain: Alqiyā: “Throw, you two”, said to the two angels (or to one, in Arab style), into Jahannam every kaffār ʿanīd: deep in disbelief and stubbornly rejecting the truth.

25.explain: Mannāʿ lil-khayr: withholding good, like zakah and what was due from his wealth. Muʿtad: transgressing against people and Allah’s limits. Murīb: doubting Allah’s promise and warning, and spreading doubt.

26.explain: …who set up another god beside Allah, worshipping what has no power at all. “Throw him into the severe punishment”: the order is repeated for emphasis.
26.why: Reportedly revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah. The ‘good’ he blocked (ayah 25) was keeping his own nephews from accepting Islam.

27.explain: His qarīn, here his devil companion, disowns him: “Our Lord, I did not make him rebel; he was already far astray.” In another view this companion is the recording angel, denying he added anything.

28.explain: Allah says: lā takhtaṣimū ladayya, do not argue before Me; it is useless now. I sent the warning ahead, through messengers and books, so the proof against you is already established.

29.explain: Mā yubaddalu al-qawlu ladayya: My word does not change, and what I have decided will happen. Wa mā ana bi-ẓallām: I never wrong My servants; I punish only for real sins.

30.explain: Allah asks Jahannam, “Are you full?” It says, “Hal min mazīd?” Either it asks for more until Allah places His Foot on it and it says “Enough!”, or it means “I’m full; there’s no room.”

31.explain: Uzlifat: Paradise is brought close to the muttaqīn, the righteous, ghayra baʿīd, not far off, so they can see it before they enter.

32.explain: “This is what you were promised”, for every awwāb, who keeps returning to Allah in repentance, and ḥafīẓ, who guards Allah’s commands, His limits and his covenant with Him.

33.explain: Who feared ar-Raḥmān bil-ghayb: in private where no one saw, without ever seeing Him. And came with a qalb munīb, a heart that keeps turning to Him in humility.

34.explain: Udkhulūhā bi-salām: enter it in peace, safe from every harm, greeted with salām. Dhālika yawmu al-khulūd: the Day of forever, with no death and no leaving.

35.explain: They have whatever they wish. Wa ladaynā mazīd: with Us is more, beyond anything they could think to ask for, reported to include looking at Allah’s noble Face.

36.explain: Kam ahlaknā: how many generations Allah destroyed, stronger than Quraysh. They naqqabū, roamed and built across the land, yet found no maḥīṣ, no escape, when the punishment came.

37.explain: That is dhikrā, a reminder, for whoever has a qalb, a living, understanding heart, or alqā as-samʿ, lends an ear, wa huwa shahīd, with the heart present, not wandering.

38.explain: Allah made the heavens, the earth and everything between in six days, and no lughūb, no tiredness, touched Him. The One who made all that without effort can easily raise the dead.
38.why: Reportedly revealed in reply to some Jews who said Allah created everything in six days and then rested on the seventh, Saturday. This ayah denies that He ever tires.

39.explain: Fa-ṣbir: bear what they say, their insults and denial. Sabbiḥ bi-ḥamdi rabbik: glorify with praise, meaning prayer, before sunrise (Fajr) and before sunset (ʿAṣr). The Prophet ﷺ urged guarding these two prayers.

40.explain: Glorify Him in part of the night too, and adbār as-sujūd, after the prostrations: either the tasbīḥ said after each obligatory prayer, or the two rakʿahs after Maghrib.

41.explain: Wa-stamiʿ: listen for the Day the munādī, the Caller, calls from a place that is near, so everyone hears it close by. The Caller is the angel Isrāfīl, reportedly calling from the Rock in Jerusalem.

42.explain: The Day they hear aṣ-ṣayḥah, the Blast of the Horn, bil-ḥaqq, in truth, with no doubt left. Dhālika yawmu al-khurūj: the Day of coming out of the graves.

43.explain: Innā naḥnu nuḥyī wa numīt: Allah alone gives life and causes death, and to Him is the final return, where each person is repaid for their deeds.

44.explain: The earth splits open off them and they rush out, sirāʿā, hurrying to answer the Caller. The Prophet ﷺ said the earth would open first for him. Gathering everyone is yasīr, easy for Allah.

45.explain: Allah knows what they say, so don’t grieve. Mā anta ʿalayhim bi-jabbār: you are not there to force them into faith (this came before fighting was ordered). Fa-dhakkir: remind with the Quran whoever fears the warning.
45.why: Reportedly, people said, “O Messenger of Allah, if only you would warn us,” and the words “so remind with the Quran whoever fears My threat” came down.
